profileText: A Delegate from New York; born in Pelham Manor, N.Y., July 7, 1753; graduated from King's College (now Columbia University), New York City, 1770; studied law; admitted to the bar and practiced in New York City and Westchester County, N.Y.; served in the Revolutionary War, lieutenant, New York volunteers, in 1776; deputy judge advocate, Continental Army, in 1777; member of the New York assembly, 1779-1781; judge advocate general, army, 1781-1783; member of General George Washington's staff at the British evacuation of the city of New York in 1783; member of the New York state assembly, 1784-1786; regent of the University of the State of New York, 1784-1787; surrogate of Westchester County, N.Y., March 13, 1787-October 31, 1800; Delegate to the Confederation Congress, 1789; died on May 1, 1811, in Pelham Manor, N.Y.; interment in St. Paul's Churchyard, Eastchester (now in the Bronx), N.Y.
